reference: Runnable metadata contracts use Bash's documented type/help builtins and the registered dhcpd synopsis/help strings in /source/loadables/dhcpd.c. Offline operation contracts use a fixed BOOTP/DHCP request encoded from the RFC 2131 header/cookie/options layout, RFC 2131 response fields and option codes, and the documented lease-file format; all files are relative to the runner's private fixture directory. There is no matching GNU DHCP server or packet-parser CLI for byte-for-byte parity. Network exchanges and hook execution remain deferred.
coverage: Bash reports dhcpd as an enabled shell builtin.
Short and long help metadata expose the registered synopsis and documented interfaces.
Offline parse-req decodes a fixed DHCPDISCOVER transaction ID, client address and hostname option.
Offline respond builds an OFFER with independently specified BOOTP fields and DHCP options from a relative fixture config.
Lease add/list/remove cover the documented lease record format, TTL range, replacement for one MAC and missing-record status using a relative file.
Deferred operation coverage identifies requirements for DHCP exchange, relay/PXE behavior, DECLINE/RELEASE and hooks.
exclusions: There is no matching GNU DHCP CLI for these custom subcommands, so offline operations are honest contract tests rather than GNU parity.
No server socket, real network target, host path, service, installed credentials or external lease-exec command is used.
The deferred server and hook cases are not executed and do not count as passes.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves dhcpd as a builtin without invoking any dhcpd subcommand.
Check the registered short synopsis through Bash help metadata; the expected fragment comes from dhcpd_struct.short_doc in the pinned source.
Check representative long-help text against the independent dhcpd_doc strings in the pinned source, including parser, lease, and PXE usage.
cases.script:
doc=$(help dhcpd)
[[ $doc == *'Minimal DHCPv4 server (RFC 2131): one pool, single subnet.'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'dhcpd parse-req HEX [-V VAR]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'dhcpd lease-add MAC IP [-l LEASEDB] [-t TTL]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'proxy-dhcp on|off.'* ]]
printf 'long-help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Decode a fixed RFC 2131 BOOTREQUEST with DHCPDISCOVER, transaction ID 0x1234abcd, a six-byte client address and hostname option 12.
cases.script:
headzeros=
tailzeros=
for ((i=0; i<20; i++)); do headzeros+=00; done
for ((i=0; i<202; i++)); do tailzeros+=00; done
packet="010106001234abcd${headzeros}020000000001${tailzeros}638253633501010c06636c69656e74ff"
parsed=$(dhcpd parse-req "$packet")
[[ $parsed == 'msg_type=DISCOVER  xid=0x1234abcd  chaddr=02:00:00:00:00:01  hostname=client' ]]
printf 'parse-contract-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Build an offline DHCPOFFER from a fixed DISCOVER and one-address relative config, checking the transaction ID, offered/server addresses, cookie, total packet length and RFC option fields.
Exercise lease-add/list/remove on the relative private fixture file, checking record fields, numeric TTL output, same-MAC replacement and missing-MAC failure.
cases.script:
dhcpd lease-add 02:00:00:00:00:01 192.0.2.100 -l leases -t 600
listing=$(dhcpd lease-list -l leases)
IFS=' ' read -r mac ip expiry_field remaining_field hostname <<< "$listing"
[[ $mac == 02:00:00:00:00:01 && $ip == 192.0.2.100 && $hostname == hostname=- ]]
expiry=${expiry_field#expiry=}
remaining=${remaining_field#remaining=}
[[ $expiry =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $remaining =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
(( expiry > 0 && remaining >= 590 && remaining <= 600 ))
dhcpd lease-add 02:00:00:00:00:01 192.0.2.101 -l leases -t 600
listing=$(dhcpd lease-list -l leases)
[[ $listing == '02:00:00:00:00:01 192.0.2.101 '* ]]
[[ $listing != *192.0.2.100* && $listing != *$'\n'* ]]
dhcpd lease-remove 02:00:00:00:00:01 -l leases
[[ -z $(dhcpd lease-list -l leases) ]]
if dhcpd lease-remove 02:00:00:00:00:01 -l leases; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'lease-crud-contract-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Cover the serve/run path through bounded DHCPDISCOVER/OFFER and DHCPREQUEST/ACK exchanges, pool allocation, lease persistence and wrapper state-directory handling.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed private DHCP socket mock with an isolated client, deterministic packet capture and temporary config/lease paths. Current instructions prohibit network activity and server invocation; UDP/67 behavior is not exercised.

cases.purpose: Cover giaddr-based subnet selection and reply routing, option-82 echo, ProxyDHCP on UDP/4011, and configured PXE options.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable DHCP relay/client fixture or reviewed socket mock that can independently inspect giaddr, option 82, proxy replies and PXE option 43/66/67. Network activity is prohibited in this run, so these server paths are not invoked.

cases.purpose: Cover DECLINE quarantine, RELEASE lease removal and lease-exec commit/release environment variables without allowing an uncontrolled child command.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed packet/clock and child-process mock. The fixture must inject DECLINE and RELEASE packets, observe the quarantine interval deterministically, and replace lease-exec with a bounded recording stub; no packets or hook commands are run here.
